content: Penguins are a group of aquatic, flightless birds. They are adapted for life in the water, with their wings evolved into flippers that allow them to swim effectively. Although they are birds, penguins cannot fly in the air because their wing structure and body weight are optimized for swimming rather than air flight. Their bones are denser than those of other birds, reducing buoyancy and making it easier to dive into the water to catch their prey. They are well-adapted to their life in water and on land but do not have the capability to fly like other birds.
